p.src: Now Yang Zhi, Sun An, and Bian Xiang were pursuing Xi Sheng when they reached the flank of Mount Yique. They did not suspect that an enemy commander lay in ambush behind the slope; leading ten thousand cavalrymen, he suddenly charged out and fought a fierce battle with Yang Zhi and the others. Xi Sheng escaped and led his battered remnants back into the city. Sun An fought with desperate courage and slew two enemy commanders, but his force was hopelessly outnumbered, and all thousand-odd armored horsemen were driven by the enemy into a deep ravine. The ravine was enclosed on all sides by sheer cliffs and had no other way out. The enemy hauled up timber and rocks and completely blocked its mouth. The enemy returned to the city and reported the matter to Gong Duan. Gong Duan sent two thousand troops to guard the mouth of the ravine; even if Yang Zhi, Sun An, and the others had grown wings, they could not have flown out.

p.src: Leaving Yang Zhi and the others trapped for the moment, let us speak of Lu Junyi and his men. Their defeat of Xi Sheng's Six-Flower Formation owed much to Ma Ling's art of the golden brick, with which he struck down untold numbers of enemy soldiers, as well as to the valor of all the commanders. They won a complete victory, slew three fierce enemy generals, and pressed their advantage to seize Dragon Gate Pass. They took more than ten thousand heads and captured countless horses, suits of armor, gongs, and drums, while the enemy troops retreated into the city. When Lu Junyi mustered and counted his forces, only Yang Zhi, Sun An, and Bian Xiang—the vanguard commanders—and their thousand troops were missing. Lu Junyi at once ordered Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Zou Yuan, and Zou Run each to lead a thousand men and search along four separate routes, but by sunset they had found no trace or word of the missing force.

p.src: The next day, Lu Junyi kept his army in place and again ordered Xie Zhen and the others to go out searching. Xie Bao led one detachment onward, clinging to vines and creepers as they climbed mountains and crossed ridges, until they reached the highest peak east of Mount Yique. Looking west from the ridge, he dimly made out a cluster of men and horses in a deep ravine below, but the dense forest concealed them, and he could not see clearly. Moreover, the gulf in height was so great that no shouted call could be heard. Xie Bao led his soldiers down the mountain to seek out local residents and ask them, but every household there had fled elsewhere because of the warfare. At last they reached a level clearing in the deepest and most secluded hollow, where they finally found a few families of impoverished peasants. At the sight of so many soldiers and horses, the villagers were thrown into a panic. Xie Bao said, “We are soldiers of the imperial court, come here to suppress and capture the bandits.” When the people heard that they were government troops, they became even more alarmed. Xie Bao soothed them with kind words, saying, “Our commanders and troops serve under Vanguard Commander Song.” The people said, “Do you mean Vanguard Commander Song, who slew the Tartars, captured Tian Hu, and never harassed the countryside?” Xie Bao replied, “The very same.” The peasants knelt and bowed, saying, “No wonder you generals have not come to seize our chickens or carry off our dogs! Two years ago, government troops also came here to suppress the bandits, but those soldiers plundered us just like brigands. That is why we fled and took refuge in this place. Now that you have come, General, we can see the light of day once more.” Xie Bao asked them about the whereabouts of Yang Zhi and his thousand men, and also about the deep ravine west of the ridge. They all replied, “That ravine is called Anliaohong, and there is only one road leading into it.” The peasants then guided Xie Bao and his men to the mouth of the ravine, just as the two detachments led by Zou Yuan and Zou Run arrived there in the course of their search. Joining their forces, they scattered the enemy guards and advanced together to remove the timber and rocks. Xie Bao and Zou Yuan then led their troops into the ravine. p.src: Yang Zhi, Sun An, Bian Xiang, and their thousand soldiers, their horses spent and the men exhausted, were all beneath the trees, sitting helplessly and awaiting death. When they saw Xie Bao and the approaching troops, they all leaped for joy and cheered. Xie Bao distributed the dry provisions he had brought among Yang Zhi and the others, so that they might first stave off their hunger. When they had eaten, the entire force left the ravine together. Xie Bao asked the peasants to accompany them to the main camp and meet Vanguard Commander Lu. Lu Junyi was overjoyed and took out silver and grain to relieve the impoverished people; the peasants knocked their heads upon the ground in gratitude, thanked him over and over, and departed. Afterward, Xie Zhen's detachment also returned to camp. As evening had fallen, they rested for the night, and nothing further occurred.

p.src: Early the next morning, as Lu Junyi and Zhu Wu were deploying the troops to take the city, a mounted scout came racing in to report that Wang Qing had sent his false commander-in-chief Du Xue, with twelve officers and twenty thousand troops, to the rescue; they were already only thirty li away. On hearing the report, Lu Junyi ordered Zhu Wu, Yang Zhi, Sun Li, Shan Tinggui, and Wei Dingguo, together with Qiao Daoqing and Ma Ling, to command twenty thousand troops and form ranks before the main camp, there to withstand any sortie by the rebels inside the city; he ordered Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Mu Chun, and Xue Yong to command five thousand troops and guard the mountain camp. Lu Junyi himself led the remaining officers and thirty-five thousand troops out to meet Du Xue. At this, Yan Qing the Wanderer reported, “Master, it would be unwise for you to take the field in person today.” Lu Junyi asked, “Why is that?” Yan Qing replied, “Last night I had an ominous dream.” Lu Junyi said, “Dreams are hardly things one can trust. Having pledged my life to the nation, I can no longer concern myself with gain or peril.” Yan Qing said, “If you are resolved to go, master, then please assign me five hundred infantrymen and let me attend to something on my own.” Lu Junyi laughed. “Little Yi, what are you planning to do?” Yan Qing replied, “Never mind that, master. Just assign them to me.” Lu Junyi said, “Very well, I shall give them to you and see what you accomplish!” He immediately assigned five hundred infantrymen to Yan Qing. Yan Qing led them away. Lu Junyi could not stop chuckling to himself. He led the assembled officers and troops out of the main camp and passed by Pingquan Bridge. Pingquan abounded in curious stones and had once been the estate of Li Deyu of the Tang dynasty. There Lu Junyi saw Yan Qing leading his men in felling trees. Though Lu Junyi found it amusing, he was hurrying to battle and had no time to question him. The army went ten li west of Longmen Pass, formed ranks facing west, and waited. After two hours, the rebel army finally arrived. The two armies faced each other, beating drums and raising battle cries. From the western ranks, the lieutenant Wei He brandished a long-shafted saber and spurred his horse to the fore. From the Song ranks, Shan Shiqi leapt his horse forward with leveled spear and, without exchanging a word, engaged him in combat. The two horsemen fought more than thirty bouts before Shan Shiqi thrust his spear into the hind leg of Wei He’s warhorse. Its hindquarters collapsed, pitching Wei He from the saddle, and Shan Shiqi killed him with another thrust. Enraged, Feng Tai charged from the western ranks, brandishing a pair of iron maces and making straight for Shan Shiqi. After the two had fought more than ten bouts, Bian Xiang saw that Shan Shiqi was no match for Feng Tai and spurred forward, spear in hand, to assist him. But Feng Tai gave a great shout and knocked Shan Shiqi from his horse with a single blow of his mace; with another, he ended his life. He spurred his horse and brandished his sword to meet Bian Xiang, but Bian Xiang was fiercer still. The instant Feng Tai’s horse came near, Bian Xiang roared and drove his spear into Feng Tai’s heart, killing him beneath his horse. Both armies erupted in shouts. Seeing two of his officers fall in succession, Du Xue, commander of the western army, felt his heart blaze like fire and rage smoke within him. Leveling an eighteen-foot serpent spear, he galloped out to fight in person. Lu Junyi, commander of the Song army, likewise rode out himself. He and Du Xue fought fifty bouts without either gaining the advantage. Du Xue’s serpent spear struck with uncanny and unpredictable skill. Seeing that Vanguard Lu could not prevail, Sun An brandished his sword, spurred his horse, and rode in to help. The rebel general Zhuo Mao galloped out to meet him, wielding a wolf-toothed club. They had fought no more than four or five bouts when Sun An summoned his divine prowess and cut Zhuo Mao down from his horse with one stroke of his sword. Sun An wheeled his horse, charged forward, and swung his sword at Du Xue. Du Xue, seeing that Sun An had slain Zhuo Mao, was caught unprepared. Sun An’s sword flashed down and severed his right arm, sending him tumbling from his horse; Lu Junyi then finished him with a thrust of his spear.

p.src: Suddenly, a body of cavalry burst from a slanting side path to the southwest. At their head rode a general of coarse, dark, hideous appearance, with a shock of short, disheveled hair, an iron Daoist crown on his head, a campaign robe on his body, and a coal-red horse beneath him. Sword in hand, he directed his troops, wheeling and bounding as they came racing forward. Seeing that they wore rebel uniforms, Lu Junyi and his men drove their troops forward in a massed charge. The general did not engage them. Instead, he muttered a few incantations and slashed his sword toward the southern station of Fire. In an instant, flames spurted from his mouth. In moments, fire roared up from the empty ground and dense smoke billowed, sweeping toward the Song army. Lu Junyi could not flee quickly enough. The Song army was routed, abandoning gongs, drums, and horses as the men scattered wildly. Those who could not escape in time were scorched from head to face. More than five thousand soldiers were killed. The officers guarded Lu Junyi as they fled to Pingquan Bridge. The soldiers scrambled to be first onto the bridge, and in an instant their crushing weight made it collapse. Fortunately, Yan Qing had felled trees and had just finished laying pontoon bridges on both sides of the bridge. The soldiers were able to cross, and twenty thousand survived. Lu Junyi and Bian Xiang, both on horseback, had fallen behind. As they reached the bridge, the rebel general caught up and spat a mouthful of flame at Bian Xiang. Bian Xiang’s whole body burst into flames. Badly burned, he fell from his horse and was killed by the rebel soldiers. Thanks to the pontoon bridge, Lu Junyi managed to gallop away to safety.

p.src: The rebel general led his troops onward in pursuit, but the vanguard had already sent word to Qiao Daoqing. Qiao Daoqing rode out alone with sword in hand and confronted the rebel general. When the rebel general saw Qiao Daoqing approaching, he again slashed his sword toward the south, and the flames blazed even more fiercely than before. Qiao Daoqing formed a hand seal and chanted a spell, then pointed his sword toward the northern station of Water and invoked the art of the “Divine Samadhi Water.” In a flash, hundreds upon thousands of streams of black vapor flew forward to meet the flames, transforming into cataracts and flying springs, like countless measures of lustrous pearls and fragments of jade. They poured over the rebel general and extinguished his sorcerous fire. Seeing his sorcery broken, the rebel general wheeled his horse and fled. His mount stepped on a wet stone, lost its footing behind, and threw him from the saddle. Qiao Daoqing galloped after him and cut him in two with one sweep of his sword. Of the five thousand cavalrymen, more than five hundred were thrown down and injured. Holding his sword aloft, Qiao Daoqing shouted, “If you are willing to surrender, you may all keep your donkey heads!” Seeing Qiao Daoqing’s wondrous powers, the rebels all dismounted, cast down their weapons, and prostrated themselves to beg for their lives. Qiao Daoqing soothed them with kindly words, cut off the rebel general’s head, and led the surrendered rebels to Vanguard Lu to present his victory. Lu Junyi thanked him profusely and also praised Yan Qing for his service. The officers questioned the surrendered rebels and learned that the sorcerer’s surname was Kou and his given name was Mie, and that he habitually burned men with enchanted fire. Because of his hideous appearance, people called him the “Demon King of Venomous Flame.” He had once helped Wang Qing in his rebellion, but then vanished for two years. Recently he returned to Nanfeng and said, “The Song army is powerful; let me go and destroy it.” Wang Qing had therefore sent him racing to this place. When Gong Duan and Xi Sheng saw that the relief force had been defeated, they dared not come out to fight and merely reinforced their troops and held the city fast.

p.src: That night, at the second watch, Qiao Daoqing came forth, wielded his sword, and performed his magic. In moments a fog arose and completely shrouded the whole circuit of the Western Capital; the defenders could not distinguish anything even at arm’s length, nor could one man see to another. Under cover of darkness, the Song troops climbed from their swift-moving siege wagons onto the battlements. At the sound of a cannon, the dense fog suddenly cleared and light returned. Song soldiers stood on every side of the walls; each drew out kindling, lit torches, and illuminated the heights and depths as brightly as day. As for the defenders— they had already been stunned senseless with terror and could not move. The Song troops drew their weapons and cut them down, while countless rebel soldiers fell from the walls to their deaths. Gong Duan and Xi Sheng, seeing the sudden upheaval, hastily led troops to the rescue, but the Song army had already seized all four gates. Lu Junyi drove his forces into the city in a great surge. Gong Duan and Xi Sheng were both killed amid the melee. All the remaining deputy commanders, officers, and chieftains surrendered, together with thirty thousand soldiers, while not so much as a hair of the common people was harmed.

p.src: At daybreak, Lu Junyi posted proclamations to reassure the people, recorded Qiao Daoqing’s great merit, richly rewarded the officers and men of the three armies, and sent Ma Ling to report the victory to Vanguard Commander Song. Ma Ling obeyed and departed. By evening he returned and reported, “Vanguard Commander Song and the others have been attacking Jingnan and fighting the rebels day after day. They routed the relief force from Nanfeng and captured its commander, Xie Ning. But Vanguard Commander Song, worn down by the cares of war, has fallen ill in camp, and for the past several days Military Adviser Wu has directed all military affairs.” On hearing the report, Lu Junyi grew deeply troubled. He hurriedly settled the military arrangements and entrusted the Western Capital to Qiao Daoqing and Ma Ling, who were to command its garrison. The next day, Lu Junyi took leave of Qiao Daoqing and Ma Ling and, commanding Zhu Wu and twenty other officers, departed the Western Capital and pressed urgently toward Jingnan. Before a full day had passed, his troops reached the great camp north of Jingnan, where Lu Junyi and the others entered to pay their respects.
